provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Rhyming words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify rhyming words.
The pupils should be able to produce rhyming words.

Introduction:
We have learned many words.
Today we learn words that sound alike.

Content:
Rhyming words are words that end with the same sound.
Cat and hat rhyme because they both end with 'at'.
Sun and fun rhyme because they both end with 'un'.
Let us say cat and hat together.
Now let us say sun and fun together.

Class activity:
I will say a word like 'bat'.
You will say a word that rhymes with it.
We will make a game of it.

Evaluation questions:
What does rhyming mean?
Does 'dog' rhyme with 'fog'?
Can you find a word that rhymes with 'ball'?

Summary:
Rhyming words are fun to learn.
They help us read better.

topics.title: Opposites
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify opposite words.
The pupils should be able to match opposite words.

Introduction:
We know big and small.
Today we learn more opposites.

Content:
Opposites are words with opposite meanings.
Big and small are opposites.
Up and down are opposites.
A big house is not a small house.
When I go up I am not going down.

Class activity:
I will call out a word.
You will call out its opposite.
We will do it with actions too.

Evaluation questions:
What is the opposite of 'hot'?
Is 'day' the opposite of 'night'?
Show me the opposite of 'up'.

Summary:
Opposites help us describe things better.
We use them every day.

topics.title: My body words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name body parts.
The pupils should be able to point to body parts.

Introduction:
We use our body to play.
Today we learn their names.

Content:
Our body has many parts.
We have a head on top.
We have hands to clap.
We have eyes to see.
We have ears to hear.
We have legs to walk.

Class activity:
I will say a body part.
You will point to it on your body.
We will sing a song about our body.

Evaluation questions:
What do we use to see?
Where is your ear?
Show me your hand.

Summary:
We must care for our body parts.
They help us do many things.

topics.title: Family words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name family members.
The pupils should be able to draw family members.

Introduction:
We all have a family.
Today we learn family words.

Content:
Family are people we love.
Mummy is a family member.
Daddy is a family member.
Sister is a family member.
Brother is a family member.
We live with our family.

Class activity:
We will draw our family.
Then we will label each person.
Mummy, daddy, sister, brother.

Evaluation questions:
Who is in your family?
What do we call our male parent?
Draw your sister.

Summary:
Family is very important.
We love our family.

topics.title: Classroom words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name classroom objects.
The pupils should be able to label classroom objects.

Introduction:\ We come to school every day.
Today we learn classroom words.

Content:
Our classroom has many things.
We sit on a chair.
We write on a desk.
We read a book.
The teacher writes on the board.

Class activity:
I will point to something in the classroom.
You will say what it is.
Then we will label pictures of classroom things.

Evaluation questions:
Where do we sit?
What do we read?
Show me the board.

Summary:
We must take care of our classroom.
It helps us learn.

topics.title: Colours and number words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name colours.
The pupils should be able to count numbers.

Introduction:
We see colours all around us.
We use numbers every day.

Content:
Colours are what we see.
Red is like a ripe tomato.
Blue is like the sky.
Numbers help us count.
One, two, three are the first numbers.

Class activity:
I will show colour cards.
You will say the colour name.
Then we will count objects in the classroom.

Evaluation questions:
What colour is the sky?
How many eyes do you have?
Count three pencils.

Summary:
Colours make our world beautiful.
Numbers help us count things.

topics.title: Reading short sentences
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read short sentences.
The pupils should be able to understand short sentences.

Introduction:
We have learned many words.
Today we put words together.

Content:
A sentence is a group of words.
It makes sense together.
'I can see a big bus' is a sentence.
It tells us something.
We can read it together.
Then we can read it alone.

Class activity:
We will read the sentence together.
Then each pupil will read it alone.
We will clap as we read.

Evaluation questions:
What is a sentence?
Can you read 'I can see a big bus'?
What can you see in the classroom?

Summary:
Reading sentences is fun.
It helps us learn to read.

topics.title: Question words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name question words.
The pupils should be able to ask simple questions.

Introduction:
Sometimes we want to know things.
Today we learn question words.

Content:
Question words help us ask.
What is used to ask about things.
Where is used to ask about places.
Who is used to ask about people.
We can use them to ask questions.

Class activity:
I will model asking questions.
What is your name?
Where do you live?
Who is your friend?
Then pupils will ask each other.

Evaluation questions:
What question word asks about things?
Ask a question using 'where'.
Ask a question using 'who'.

Summary:
Question words help us learn.
They help us talk to others.

topics.title: Story time words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recognize story words.
The pupils should be able to read the class story.

Introduction:
Stories are fun to hear.
Today we read our class story.

Content:
A story tells us about something.
It has characters and events.
We will read our class story together.
We will point to words we know.
This helps us learn to read.

Class activity:
We will sit in a circle.
I will read the story first.
Then we will read together.
Each pupil will point to a word they know.

Evaluation questions:
What is a story?
Point to a word you know in the story.
Who is your character in the story?

Summary:
Reading stories is fun.
It helps us learn many words.

topics.title: Revision and reading celebration
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to read a page on their own.
The pupils should be able to celebrate reading.

Introduction:
We have learned so much.
Today we celebrate our reading.

Content:
We will read a page all by ourselves.
This shows how much we have learned.
Then we will have a reading celebration.
Everyone will get a certificate.
This is for our hard work.

Class activity:
Each pupil will read one page.
Then we will have a small party.
We will sing songs and clap for each other.

Evaluation questions:
Can you read a page on your own?
What did you learn this term?
How does reading make you feel?

Summary:
We are all good readers now.
Let's keep reading every day.
